title: Formal Turkish
intro: Written and official Turkish has a grammar of its own. News, notices and reports use the progressive `-mAktA(dIr)` instead of `-(I)yor`: *Toplantı devam etmektedir*. Definitions and rules put `-DIr` on almost every statement: *Giriş ücretsizdir*. Sentences are linked with *ayrıca*, *ancak* and *dolayısıyla*, letters and petitions follow set formulas, and figures, fractions and percentages are read aloud in a fixed way. You'll meet all of this in newspapers, on signs, in emails from work and in any official document.

blocks.text: News, official notices and academic writing rarely use `-(I)yor`. They use `-mAktA`, the infinitive `-mAk` with the locative: literally **in the act of doing**. With the formal `-DIr` of [A1 unit 3](gp-copula-present) on top, it gives the typical newsroom verb: *Toplantı devam etmektedir* (The meeting is in progress), *Yangın sürmektedir* (The fire is still burning).

rows.en: he, she or it is coming
he, she or it is not coming
you are not coming (plural or polite)
is he, she or it coming

blocks.text: **Endings.** The endings are those of **to be**, after the buffer y: *gelmekteyim*, *yapmaktayız*. The third person almost always adds `-DIr`: *gelmektedir*. With a plural subject, *-DIr* alone is the most common form, *Fiyatlar artmaktadır*; *-DIrlAr* appears mostly with people: *Öğrenciler sınava hazırlanmaktadırlar*. Headlines and captions drop `-DIr`: *Fiyatlar artmakta*.

**With the passive.** This style loves the passive of [B1 unit 10](gp-passive), which hides who does the work: *Konu incelenmektedir* (The matter is being examined), *Kazanın nedeni araştırılmaktadır* (The cause of the accident is being investigated), *Yeni bir plan hazırlanmaktadır* (A new plan is being prepared).
**The past.** `-mAktAydI` is the formal past progressive, common in history books and reports: *O yıllarda kent hızla büyümekteydi* (In those years the city was growing fast).

items.en: The meeting is in progress.
The authorities are examining the matter.
The patient is being treated in intensive care.
The cause of the accident is being investigated.
Flights are continuing as normal.
At that time the museum was being restored.

blocks.text: `-mAktA` belongs to writing and announcements. Said to a friend, *Şu an otobüsteyim, eve gelmekteyim* sounds like a press release; say *eve geliyorum*.

The same form, infinitive + locative, also follows verbs that take the locative: *Bu kelimeyi anlamakta zorlanıyorum* (I'm having trouble understanding this word), *Karar vermekte acele etmeyin* (Don't rush into a decision).

You met `-DIr` in [A1 unit 3](gp-copula-present) as the formal **is**: *Ali öğretmendir*. Conversation rarely uses it, but written Turkish puts it on nearly every statement of fact: definitions, rules, notices, timetables and instructions.

lines: -tır -tir -tur -tür   after f, s, t, k, ç, ş, h, p

head: Use
Example
Meaning
rows: Ankara is the capital of Turkey.
Tavla iki kişiyle oynanan bir oyun|dur.
Backgammon is a game played by two people.
The museum is closed on Mondays.
The deadline for applications is 15 March.

blocks.text: **After a tense.** `-DIr` also follows a tense in formal statements: `-mAktAdIr` (above), `-mAlIdIr` for rules, *Başvurular internet üzerinden yapılmalıdır* (Applications must be made online), and `-(y)AcAktIr` for announcements, *Toplantı saat 14.00'te yapılacaktır* (The meeting will be held at 2 p.m.).

**Var, yok, değil** become *vardır, yoktur, değildir*: *Otoparkımız yoktur* (We have no car park), *Bu belge geçerli değildir* (This document is not valid). **Gerekmek** (to be necessary) often appears as *gerekmektedir*, with a `-mA` clause as its subject ([B2 unit 4](gp-clause-as-subject)): *Formu doldurmanız gerekmektedir* (You are required to fill in the form).
**Plural subjects** usually keep the singular: *Biletler bir ay geçerlidir* (Tickets are valid for one month). For people, *-DIrlAr* is also common: *Öğrenciler sınıftadırlar*.

items.en: This ticket is valid for one month.
An ID card is required.
Smoking is forbidden in this area.
Applications must be made by 15 March.
The meeting will be held at 2 p.m.
You are required to pay a fee to apply.

blocks.text: `-DIr` follows harmony and assimilation like any suffix beginning with d: *kapalıdır*, *gereklidir*, *zorunludur*, *açıktır*, *Mart'tır*.

blocks.title: Not in conversation
blocks.text: Said aloud about a person, `-DIr` often sounds like a confident guess: *Ali şimdi evdedir* is **Ali must be home by now**. That use, and `-mIştIr` in news and encyclopedias (*Toplantı sona ermiştir*), come in [C1 unit 2](gp-dir-assumption).

sections.title: Ayrıca, ancak, dolayısıyla: formal link words

blocks.text: Formal Turkish links its sentences with words of its own. Most have an everyday partner that you already know.

head: Everyday
Formal
Meaning
rows: in order to, with the aim of

blocks.text: **Ayrıca** adds a point, usually at the start of a sentence: *Müze pazartesi günleri kapalıdır. Ayrıca bayramlarda da kapalıdır.* It can also mean **separately**: *Kahvaltı ayrıca ücretlidir* (Breakfast is charged separately).

**Ancak** is the formal **but**, after a comma or a semicolon: *Toplantı yarın yapılacaktır; ancak saati daha sonra bildirilecektir* (The meeting will be held tomorrow; however, the time will be announced later). Before a time, a number or a noun, it means **only**, **not until**: *Ancak yarın gelebilirim* (I can only come tomorrow).

**Bununla birlikte** (literally **together with this**) is **nevertheless**. **Dolayısıyla** and **bu nedenle** draw a conclusion: *Yol çalışması devam etmektedir. Bu nedenle cadde trafiğe kapalıdır* (Roadworks are under way. The street is therefore closed to traffic).

**-mAsI nedeniyle** and **-mAk amacıyla** are built from *neden* (reason) and *amaç* (aim) with the possessive and `-(y)lA` ([A1 unit 12](gp-ile)): **by its reason**, **with the aim**. *Nedeniyle* follows a noun or a `-mA` clause: *kötü hava nedeniyle*, *havanın kötü olması nedeniyle*. *Amacıyla* follows an infinitive: *trafiği azaltmak amacıyla*.

items.tr: Kar yağışı nedeniyle okullar tatil edildi.
items.seg: Kar yağışı neden|i|yle okullar tatil edildi.
items.en: Schools were closed because of the snowfall.

items.tr: Havanın kötü olması nedeniyle uçuşlar iptal edildi.
items.seg: Havanın kötü ol|ma|s|ı neden|i|yle uçuşlar iptal edildi.
items.en: Flights were cancelled because of the bad weather.

items.tr: Trafiği azaltmak amacıyla yeni bir metro hattı yapılmaktadır.
items.seg: Trafiği azaltmak amac|ı|yla yeni bir metro hattı yapılmaktadır.
items.en: A new metro line is being built in order to reduce traffic.

items.tr: Bilet fiyatları arttı; bununla birlikte yolcu sayısı düşmedi.
items.en: Ticket prices went up; nevertheless, the number of passengers did not fall.

items.tr: Toplantıya tüm çalışanlar katılmalıdır. Dolayısıyla o gün izin verilmeyecektir.
items.en: All staff must attend the meeting. Consequently, no leave will be granted that day.
Only in this way can we succeed.

blocks.text: *Nedeniyle* takes a noun or `-mA`: *olması nedeniyle*. With `-DIk`, use the everyday *için*: *olduğu için*.
*Ancak* and *bununla birlikte* are close to French **cependant**, *dolayısıyla* to **par conséquent**, *-mAk amacıyla* to **afin de** and *-mAsI nedeniyle* to **en raison de**.

sections.title: Sayın…, Saygılarımla: formal letters and requests

blocks.text: A formal email or letter follows set formulas from the first line to the last. Formal texts always use *siz*.

head: Part
Formula
Meaning
rows: Dear Ms Yılmaz, / Dear Sir or Madam,
I would be glad if you could …

blocks.text: **Rica ederim.** The heart of a formal request is the `-mA` clause of [B2 unit 4](gp-reported-commands), with *your* possessive, before *rica ederim* or *rica ederiz*: *Bilgi vermenizi rica ederim* (I would ask you to let me know), *Formu doldurup bize göndermenizi rica ederiz* (We kindly ask you to fill in the form and send it to us). The aorist *ederim* sounds more formal than *ediyorum*.

**Softer requests** use a real conditional ([B1 unit 9](gp-conditional-real)) and the aorist: *Yardımcı olursanız sevinirim* (I would be glad if you could help), *Bilgi verebilirseniz memnun olurum* (I would be pleased if you could let me know).
**Instructions** use the long imperative `-(y)InIz` of [A1 unit 12](gp-imperative): *Lütfen formu doldurunuz*, *Lütfen telefonlarınızı kapatınız*.

**The petition.** Requests to an office still often take the form of a *dilekçe*. It is addressed to the office in the dative, with no apostrophe after the name of the institution (*Kadıköy Belediye Başkanlığına*), states the request, and ends *Gereğini arz ederim* (I respectfully request the necessary action), followed by the date, the name and the signature.

blocks.tr:
Sayın Ayşe Yılmaz,

12 Mayıs'taki toplantıya katılamayacağımı üzülerek bildiririm. Toplantının notlarını bana göndermenizi rica ederim. Ayrıca bir sonraki toplantının tarihi belli olursa bilgi verebilirseniz sevinirim.

İlginiz için teşekkür ederim.

Saygılarımla,

Murat Demir

items.en: I would ask you to let me know.
Please find my application form attached.
I would be glad if you could help.
Please fill in and sign the form.

blocks.text: Emails at work often end with *İyi çalışmalar* (literally **good work**, have a good day at work) before the name, and a colleague busy at work is greeted with *Kolay gelsin* ([A2 unit 7](gp-set-wishes)).
*Sayın* goes with a surname, a full name or a title: *Sayın Yılmaz*, *Sayın Ayşe Yılmaz*, *Sayın Yetkili*. With a first name alone, the polite form is *Ayşe Hanım* or *Murat Bey*.

sections.title: Yarım, buçuk, üçte bir, yüzde elli: figures aloud

blocks.text: **Half** has three words. *Yarım* is an adjective before a noun: *yarım ekmek* (half a loaf), *yarım saat* (half an hour). *Buçuk* follows a number: *iki buçuk saat* (two and a half hours), *saat üç buçuk* (half past three, [A1 unit 11](gp-telling-time)). *Yarı* is a noun, **half of**, usually with a possessive: *pastanın yarısı* (half of the cake), *öğrencilerin yarısı* (half of the students).

head: Word
Where
Example
rows: *yarım kilo peynir* (half a kilo of cheese)
*bir buçuk saat* (an hour and a half)

blocks.text: **Fractions** put the denominator first, in the locative, then the numerator: *üçte bir* (one third, literally **in three, one**), *dörtte üç* (three quarters), *onda bir* (one tenth). Of a group, add the genitive and a possessive: *nüfusun üçte biri* (a third of the population), *öğrencilerin dörtte üçü* (three quarters of the students).

**Percentages.** *Yüzde* (literally **in a hundred**) comes **before** the number, and so does the sign: *%50* is *yüzde elli*. Of something, again with the genitive and a possessive: *nüfusun yüzde altmışı* (sixty percent of the population). A suffix on the written figure follows the last word said, after an apostrophe: *%40'ı* (*yüzde kırkı*), *%50'si* (*yüzde ellisi*).

**Reading figures aloud.** As you saw in [A1 unit 11](gp-numbers), decimals take a comma, read *virgül*, and thousands a dot: *3,5* is *üç virgül beş*, *1.250.000* is *bir milyon iki yüz elli bin*. A billion is *milyar*: *2,5 milyar* is *iki buçuk milyar* or *iki virgül beş milyar*. **Times as much** uses *kat*: *iki katı* (twice as much), *Fiyatlar iki katına çıktı* (Prices doubled).

blocks.caption: Written and said
head: Written
Said

bir milyon iki yüz elli bin

items.en: I'm coming in half an hour.
The meeting lasted an hour and a half.
The children ate half of the cake.
A third of the students failed the exam.
Sixty percent of the population lives in cities.

items.tr: Fiyatlar bir yılda iki katına çıktı.
items.seg: Fiyatlar bir yılda iki kat|ı|n|a çıktı.
items.en: Prices doubled in a year.

blocks.text: Turkish writes the percent sign before the number, as it is said: *%50*, *yüzde elli*.
*İkide bir* is not a fraction. It means **every so often, all the time**: *İkide bir telefonuna bakıyor* (She keeps checking her phone).

summary: `-mAktA(dIr)` is the formal progressive of news, notices and reports: *devam etmektedir*, *incelenmektedir*; the past is *-mAktAydI*.
Written Turkish puts `-DIr` on definitions, rules and notices: *Giriş ücretsizdir*, *Kask takmak zorunludur*; also after tenses: *yapılmalıdır*, *yapılacaktır*.
Formal link words: *ayrıca* (also), *ancak* (but; only), *bununla birlikte* (nevertheless), *dolayısıyla* and *bu nedenle* (therefore).
*-mAsI nedeniyle* is **because of**, *-mAk amacıyla* **in order to**: *kötü hava nedeniyle*, *trafiği azaltmak amacıyla*.
Formal letters: *Sayın* + surname, *-mAnızı rica ederim*, *-(y)AbilIrsAnIz sevinirim*, *Saygılarımla*.
*Yarım* before a noun, *buçuk* after a number, *yarı* + possessive for **half of**.
Fractions and percentages: *üçte bir*, *dörtte üç*, *yüzde elli* (*%50*); of a group, genitive + possessive: *nüfusun yüzde altmışı*.
